sentences.t: Every year I redo my desk setup, and every year I tell myself this is the last time.
This year I think I actually mean it, so let's go through what changed and why.
First, the desk itself is the same oak top I've had for three years, but I finally got rid of the motorized frame.
I tracked it, and I stood up at this desk maybe four times last year, so it was a very expensive wobble.
Now it's a fixed frame at exactly the right height for me, and it's rock solid.
Monitor-wise, I went from two screens down to one big one, and that was the biggest productivity change of the whole year.
With two screens, I always had something distracting on the second one, chat, email, a video I was half watching.
With one, whatever I'm working on is the only thing in front of me.
Keyboard is a low-profile mechanical with really quiet switches, because I record voiceovers at this desk and the clacky one was showing up in the audio.
Before we get to lighting, which was the other big change, a quick word from the two sponsors of this video.
First up, this video is sponsored by Notion.
Notion is one workspace for your notes, your tasks, your docs, and your projects, instead of having them spread across five different apps.
I plan my whole week in it, and it's the reason I stopped losing track of client deadlines.
And with Notion AI built in, you can ask it things like, what did I promise in last month's meeting notes, and it actually finds it.
Try Notion for free at notion.com/kai, the link is in the description.
And our second sponsor today is Ridge, which, yes, is a wallet, and I promise it's relevant to sitting at a desk.
I used to keep this giant leather wallet in my back pocket, and sitting at a desk all day with it was genuinely giving me back pain.
The Ridge is this slim aluminum wallet that holds up to twelve cards and has RFID blocking built in.
It lives in my front pocket now, and I barely notice it's there.
It's got a lifetime warranty too, so it's probably the last wallet I'll ever buy.
Use code KAI at ridge.com/kai for up to forty percent off.
Okay, so, lighting.
I got rid of the overhead light completely and replaced it with a lamp behind the monitor that bounces off the wall.
Way less eye strain, and on camera it looks a hundred times better.
There's also a little warm lamp on the shelf, mostly because it makes me happy.
Cable management, I'm not going to pretend it's perfect, but everything runs through one tray under the desk, so from the front you see one cable.
That one cable is the monitor, and I've made peace with it.
And the last thing is the plant, which I have now kept alive for eleven months, a personal record.
If you've got questions about any of the gear, leave them in the comments and I'll answer as many as I can.
Thanks for watching, see you next time.
